newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary share market ends up, eyes on MOL.
newsitem.headline: Hungary share market ends up, eyes on MOL.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed on Wednesday, apparently receiving only little help from a rally on Wall Street, pushing the BUX index a shade higher.
According to preliminary data the BUX index finished at 5,840.65 points, up 37.39.
Analysts and traders said that shares in oil company MOL were in focus as market participants were preparing for its upcoming global placement.

"The MOL issue is focusing people's attention on Hungary again, that's good for Hungary and the strength of the Hungarian market is good for the MOL issue," said Stephen O'Sullivan, analyst at MC-BBL Securities in London.
MOL shares closed at 3,195 forints, down 30.
"Investors went short in MOL shares in London (on SEAQ) and its price on Budapest followed," said Balazs Szabo of Eastbrokers.
The market was expecting an issue price in MOL shares below its current market price and traders expected a further decline in its price.
"I expect it (MOL) to continue to go down on Thursday," Szabo said.
Elsewhere on the market pharmaceuticals stocks went mostly upwards with Richter rising 400 forints to 12,300 and Human gaining 85 forints to 2,985, but Egis dipping 30 forints to 11,850.
Chemicals TVK and Borsodchem firmed 40 forints each to 2,750 forints and 6,540 forints, respectively.
Clothes retailer Aranypok whose shareholders approved the payout of a seven percent dividend on the 1996 earnings, eased 50 forints to end at 7,500.
Analyst said the market's short-term outlook was flat.

"Our view is that the market is going to be fairly flat," O'Sullivan said. "There's a firm undertone, they're not going to go down, but obviously after the all-time high reached on Monday, there has been profit-taking, which is not surprising."
